question.text: Which option best summarises the violations found in the SEBI vs SHCIL (Case 11.2) DDP matter?

answer.text: Non-maintenance of records, registration of ineligible FPIs, DDP manual discrepancies, KYC/demat-form non-compliance, fit and proper check failures, failure to segregate activities and maintain necessary infrastructure, and delay in forwarding the internal-control audit report
Only failure to maintain necessary infrastructure
Only non-maintenance of records and delayed filing of returns
Only registration of ineligible FPIs and charging excess fees

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook records the SHCIL matter as multi-violation: non-maintenance of records and documents, registration of ineligible FPIs, discrepancies in the DDP manual, non-compliance with KYC and demat forms, fit and proper check failures, failure to segregate activities and maintain necessary infrastructure, and delay in forwarding the internal-control audit report. The Trap: The single-issue option choices understate the case; SHCIL was held responsible for a cluster of compliance failures spanning records, eligibility, KYC, fit-and-proper, infrastructure and audit-report timing. Note: The SHCIL summary is useful as a checklist: a DDP must control records, eligibility filters, KYC, infrastructure, segregation and audit-report submission together - failure in any one of these can compound the regulatory exposure.
